formation.note: Year of the proposal, used as a lower bound for the collaboration formation.
formation.quote: In 1971, we submitted the SLAC-LBL Proposal (Larsen et al. 1971) using the Mark I detector at SPEAR.

intervals.label: SPEAR data taking
intervals.locator: Richter Nobel lecture, section 2.5; end from the SLAC AHRO Mark page (1977: dismantled and removed from SPEAR)
intervals.note: Richter (December 1976) says the Mark I would be replaced at SPEAR by the Mark II in the fall of 1977; the SLAC archives page gives 1977 for its dismantling and removal.
intervals.quote: The Mark I magnetic detector was ready to begin taking data in February 1973.

intervals.label: dismantled and removed from SPEAR
intervals.locator: SLAC AHRO "MARK" page, detectors table (Mark I)

summary.plain: The SLAC and Lawrence Berkeley Laboratory physicists who built and ran the Mark I detector at SPEAR, including the groups of Burton Richter, Martin Perl, Gerson Goldhaber, George Trilling and William Chinowsky.
summary.technical: SLAC-LBL collaboration: SLAC Group C (B. Richter, J. Rees) and Group E (M. Perl, G. Feldman) with an LBL group (W. Chinowsky, G. Goldhaber, G. Trilling), later joined by others; discoverers of the J/ψ (1974) and the τ (1975).
